title: Elliptic integral identities derived from Coxeter's integrals
summary: We revisit the classical integrals introduced by Coxeter, not to recalculate their well-known exact values, but to use them as a tool to derive elliptic integral identities. By embedding Coxeter's first integral into a one-parameter family $$ I(λ)=\int_{0}^{π/2} \arccos\!\left(\frac{\cosθ}{1+λ\cosθ}\right)\,dθ, $$ and differentiating with respect to the parameter \(λ\), we show that the derivative $I'(λ)$ can be expressed as an elliptic-type integral. Integrating $I'(λ)$ between 0 and 2 yields the identity $$ \int_0^2 \int_0^{π/2} \frac{\cos^2θ} {(1+s\cosθ)\sqrt{(1+s\cosθ)^2-\cos^2θ}} \,dθ\,…
